answer: Trust propagates through an attestation graph by bounded random walks, so influence must cross vouched edges rather than arise from identities alone. A sybil cluster like an island behind a sparse cut has low conductance: few transitions leave it relative to its internal volume. Min-cut and transitivity bounds therefore limit the walk probability reaching the cluster and cap its aggregate voting weight; extra identities cannot bypass the bottleneck, even if endorsements wander like currents around a reef.
